description: AstroMoon is a multidisciplinary team participating in NASA Space Apps Cairo. We developed an interactive Lunar South Pole landing site analysis platform for Artemis III missions using official NASA LRO/LOLA datasets.
summary: We developed Astromoon, an interactive web application and landing planner specifically designed to address the complexities of lunar exploration at the Moon's South Pole. Astromoon serves as a comprehensive tool to help mission planners and researchers analyze terrain challenges, evaluate lighting conditions, and optimize landing sites in permanently shadowed regions or high-relief areas. By providing an intuitive interface for visualizing critical lunar data, our solution directly tackles the logistical and environmental hurdles of safe spacecraft descent and resource scouting. This project is vital because unlocking the potential of the lunar South Pole—home to crucial water ice reserves—requires precise, accessible planning tools to ensure the safety and success of future crewed and robotic missions.
details:
What it does & How it works: Astromoon is an advanced, interactive web application and landing planner engineered specifically for the lunar South Pole. It provides a robust interface that allows mission planners and researchers to evaluate challenging topography, analyze solar illumination windows, and identify safe landing sites.

​Tools & Technologies: The project is robustly built using TypeScript (98.6%) for reliable and scalable logic, complemented by HTML/CSS for a responsive user interface, alongside clean configuration files. It has been successfully deployed live via GitHub to ensure high performance and accessibility.

​Benefits & Intended Impact: By converting complex geographical and environmental data into an intuitive web experience, Astromoon streamlines preliminary mission planning and enhances safety for future lunar exploration and resource scouting.
